title: Agent terminal routes (term_* backend)
what:
src/term/agent.rs, behind AG's gate (term token plus an attributed chat). JSON bodies are at most 16 KiB.
Reach (ruling 2): list, read and send work on ANY terminal opened from the web, whoever opened it. [ take over ] (423 while held) is the operator's per-terminal stop.
- POST /hub/term/a/list -> [{id, title, fg, by, chat, mine, alive, hold}]
- POST /hub/term/a/open {title?, cols? (120), rows? (32)} -> {id}
  - only if D5 = (b)
  - cwd = the chat's known_cwd
  - at most 4 open per chat
- POST /hub/term/a/read {id, lines? (screen rows, ≤ 400), max_chars? (7000), wait? {for? (literal substring ≤ 200 chars), idle_ms? (500), timeout_s ≤ 60}} -> {text, cursor, seq, alive, exit?, alt_screen}
  - the wait happens in the perch and selects on ctx.stop, so a perch stop never waits it out
- POST /hub/term/a/send {id, text? (≤ 4 KiB), keys? (≤ 32 of enter, tab, esc, backspace, up, down, left, right, home, end, pgup, pgdn, ctrl-a..ctrl-z)} -> {seq}
  - 423 while held
  - 403 with the guard's sentence when guard::refuses_term_text(text) (D9)
  - sets agent_last_ms and emits term-input
- POST /hub/term/a/close {id}: only terminals that chat opened (D5 b)
Ended terminals answer read from terms.json.
tests:
tests/term_agent.rs, using fake_eidolon's FAKE_AGENT_CALL:
- open, send 'echo hi' + enter, read waiting for 'hi'
- list shows mine:true for its own and lists every other web terminal
- another chat's agent terminal and a terminal you opened are both readable and writable (ruling 2)
- close of a terminal the chat did not open gives 403
- hold gives 423
- the term token from the test process gets 403
- the 5th open gets 409
- a read timeout is honored
- perch SIGTERM during a 60 s wait exits in under 3 s
- a term-input frame appears on the stream, and GET /hub/term shows agent_last_ms
- text naming aoide is refused when the guard is on
live_check: fake perch on PORT=48115: a fake door scripts open/send/read while `curl -N` shows the term-input and term-out frames.
risk:
- term_read hands untrusted remote text to the model.
- Agents can read every web terminal, secrets included, and that text goes to the provider.
- In yolo they type without asking.
All three are stated in the ⌨ tab and the docs.
